title: Program Status Rules: Suspension, Reinstatement and Cancellation in the Savings & Copay Assistance Programs
content:
In the Savings & Copay Assistance Programs, a program is suspended, reinstated or cancelled only on the following bases.

## Suspension

Where the program type is suspended on government coverage, the program is suspended as soon as the patient's primary coverage on file is a government class. Where the program requires commercial coverage, it is also suspended when the commercial coverage it is linked to is terminated or removed.

## Reinstatement

A suspended program is reinstated no later than the date it was suspended plus the suspension resume window days, counted in calendar days with the suspension date as day 0, and only once the cause is gone; after that it expires. The clock starts from the suspension date shown on the enrollment, and the last day of the window is allowed.

| Hypothetical program with a 60-day resume window | Result |
|---|---|
| Cause gone, reinstatement on day 60 | Reinstated (the boundary day counts) |
| Cause gone, reinstatement first sought on day 61 | Not reinstated; the program has expired |
| Day 20, cause still present | Not reinstated |

## Cancellation

A program is cancelled only at the patient's own request, which the patient confirms themselves. Cancelling keeps every benefit already applied, and refunds a membership fee only as the membership fee refund rules allow.

## Rewards points

Where the program type's fills do not earn rewards points, fills paid with the program's help earn no rewards points under the Kestrel Care Rewards rules.
